chunks: Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

“You say every night of the Month of Ramadan at the time of breaking the fast until its end: ‘All praise belongs to Allah, who helped us so we fasted, and provided for us so we broke our fast. O Allah, accept from us, help us in it, keep us safe in it, and receive it from us with ease and well-being from You. All praise belongs to Allah, who has completed for us a day of the Month of Ramadan.’”

key_terms.الْإِفْطَارِ: the time of breaking the fast
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ: praise and gratitude directed to Allah
key_terms.تَقَبَّلْ: accept; a plea for divine acceptance of worship
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the Month of Ramadan, the sacred month of fasting
key_terms.فَصُمْنَا: so we fasted; indicating divine help in completing the fast

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be recited at iftar each night in the Month of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a supplication to be recited at iftar on every night of the Month of Ramadan. It expresses gratitude to Allah for enabling the fast, asks for acceptance and well-being, and recognizes the completion of another day of worship.
